newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds sagged back again in late trade on Tuesday, undermined by renewed selling at the middle and longer end of the curve, dealers said.

The yield on the 10-year benchmark, the 5.75 percent February 2007 state loan, finished at 5.61 percent, up from 5.58 percent on Monday, when prices rose in a bund futures-inspired rally. The long 2023 bond ended three basis points up at 6.35.

But, aside from some large block deals, turnover was thin with dealers citing a lack of volatility as an extra detraction for institutional clients. A lower-than-expected Dutch April inflation figure of 1.8 percent year-on-year had little impact.

Dealers said the selling was concentrated on the longer-dated maturities but that too was dominated by a couple of large deals. The 10-year segment came under pressure from a one billion guilder issue from Kansai Electric in the morning.
At the shorter end, which attracted more support, dealers noted some early switching into five-year paper.
"At the short end there remains scope for some Dutch outperformance as the curent yield pick-up...should trigger switches from Bunds into DSLs," ABN AMRO Hoare Govett said in a report.
